To use it, put your mouth to the marked opening and blow so that the air passes over the chosen reed; the early slider type had to be set to the position for the required pitch before blowing. A beginner usually blows only the keynote needed for the song or for tuning, and need not play continuously. After use, keep it out of a pocket so that lint does not work into the gaps around the reeds; if the pitch shifts through use, the reed plate has to be replaced.

In eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Europe, churches without an organ often used one to give the starting note of a hymn. Such slider pipes are rare today, and the name has widened to cover any pitch reference device: the common form is a round free-reed aerophone, in which a brass reed vibrates and modulates the airstream while an outer chamber sounds the note; electronic button devices have appeared in recent years. It can also stand in for a tuning fork, and it serves as a clue when establishing the pitch standard of a particular place and time.

The pitch pipe is a small pitch reference device of the tuning-harmonica type; although it counts as an instrument, it is not normally used to play music. Its sounding class is aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 412.131. The early form was close to the recorder: a wooden body with a square bore and a leather-covered slider, marked with the semitones or the natural scale, blown to give a chosen note. The common modern form is a round free-reed aerophone, with metal reeds inside openings around the rim, sounded by blowing into a marked hole. It is used for tuning string instruments, for unaccompanied singing, by timpanists to give the starting note, and for calibrating the playback speed of ethnomusicological recordings.
音高笛是歐洲氣鳴樂器脈絡中的音高參考裝置，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號: The pitch pipe is a pitch reference device in the context of European aerophones, Hornbostel–Sachs number 412.131. Early on it was used in churches that had no organ, to sound the opening note of a hymn; today it is common in unaccompanied choral singing, among timpanists and for tuning string instruments, and the chromatic model supplies every semitone within an octave so that a singer can take any key. On ethnomusicological recordings, a brief pitch-pipe tone can be used to check the playback speed of a gramophone disc or cylinder.
音高笛發出的聲音清脆明亮，具有純淨而直接的音色質感。由於體積小巧，其音域相對有限: The pitch pipe's sound is crisp and bright, with a pure, direct quality. Because the instrument is small, its range is limited, usually to the upper middle register, which is enough to give any instrument an accurate reference note. The sound comes from the reed's vibration working with a narrow resonating chamber; the resonance is simple and efficient and adds little in the way of overtones. Compared with a tuner, the pitch pipe keeps a human warmth; compared with the harmonica, its tone is plainer and more exact, lacking the harmonica's warm, expressive character. The pitch pipe's voice is not full or heavy, but because the instrument is designed purely to give a reference pitch, it has a cool, objective sound, and it is a reliable helper when an ensemble tunes.
